process.obs: Converted all three docs to markdown and read each in full via the spilled-output files (steps 4-10); every UA §6(j) and prospectus governance term was in its context.
Merged all ten UA §6(j) charter items into one finding, F-5 [CRITICAL], and then rated the per-item matrix (Part IV) mostly Critical. That one choice cost five of the eight severity criteria.

Set its own 4-tier scale where Critical means 'blocks pricing or closing'. That definition pulled every closing-condition gap and every prospectus-vs-UA number mismatch up to Critical (36 findings, 7 Critical).
Generator script failed twice (steps 12-13, assertion and traceback) before the report was saved; finished in 17 steps with no pass back over the severity calls.

failures.title: ISSUE_002: Rates preferred stock authorization mismatch as High severity
failures.source: underwriting-agreement.docx §6(j)(i): IPO Charter 'not fewer than 200,000,000 Common; 10,000,000 blank-check Preferred' vs charter §4.1 (25,000,000 Preferred)
failures.deliverable: Part IV matrix item (i) Authorized capital rated 'Critical'; also folded into F-5 [CRITICAL]
failures.explanation: Facts and figures were right, but the 25M-vs-10M preferred item went into the omnibus F-5 Critical finding and was rated Critical. The expert treats it as second tier because the IPO charter will reset the number anyway. The instructions define no scale, so this is purely a calibration difference.

failures.title: ISSUE_005: Notes distinction between DGCL default rule and express requirement
failures.source: General Delaware law: DGCL §141(k)(1) (classified board: removal only for cause by default); UA §6(j)(iv): 'The IPO Charter shall provide that directors may be removed only for cause'
failures.deliverable: matrix (iv): 'Silent (DGCL §141(k) default: removal with or without cause by majority)'
failures.explanation: The report states the non-classified-board default correctly for the current charter. It never notes that once the board is classified §141(k)(1) defaults to for-cause removal, so it never explains why express language is still needed (the 66⅔% vote, and the UA's express requirement). The doctrinal nuance is missing.

failures.title: ISSUE_005: Rates director removal standard omission as High severity
failures.source: UA §6(j)(iv); charter silent on removal
failures.deliverable: matrix (iv) Removal: 'Critical: add'; F-5 [CRITICAL]
failures.explanation: Rated Critical because the item was lumped into the F-5 closing-condition finding; the expert rates it High.

failures.title: ISSUE_007: Rates supermajority amendment threshold as High severity
failures.source: UA §6(j)(viii) Supermajority Amendment 66⅔%; charter Art. X majority vote
failures.deliverable: matrix (viii) Supermajority amendment: 'Critical: add'
failures.explanation: Identified correctly but rated Critical rather than High, a result of the omnibus F-5 approach and the agent's 'blocks closing = Critical' scale.

failures.title: ISSUE_008: Rates missing classified board as High severity
failures.source: UA §6(j)(iii) three classes; charter §5.3 annual election
failures.deliverable: matrix (iii) Classified board: 'Critical: add; assign classes (F-23)'
failures.explanation: Same pattern: correct deviation, Critical instead of the expert's High.

failures.title: ISSUE_010: Rates cumulative voting omission as Medium severity
failures.source: UA §6(j)(v): 'The IPO Charter shall expressly provide that there shall be no cumulative voting'; DGCL §214 default
failures.deliverable: matrix (v) Cumulative voting: 'Silent (no cumulative voting by default under DGCL §214)' ... 'High: add express clause'
failures.explanation: The agent even noted the §214 default (it passed C-028), yet rated the item High. The expert's Medium reflects that the default already gives the same result.

failures.title: ISSUE_011: Rates over-allotment discrepancy as Medium severity
failures.source: UA §1 Option Shares 1,725,000 (15% x 11,500,000) vs prospectus 1,500,000
failures.deliverable: 'F-2 [CRITICAL] Over-allotment option: 1,500,000 shares (Prospectus) vs. 1,725,000 shares (UA)'
failures.explanation: Numbers and the correct figure were right (C-031 passed), but the agent rated it Critical as a prospectus misstatement of about $4.0M of proceeds. The expert sees an easily conformed drafting error (Medium). Defensible either way, but outside the rubric tier.

failures.title: ISSUE_012: Rates lock-up period discrepancy as High severity
failures.source: UA Exhibit C 'for a period of 180 days after the date of the Underwriting Agreement' vs UA §§1, 6(i) '180 days after the date of the final Prospectus'
failures.deliverable: 'F-7 [CRITICAL] Lock-up form (Exhibit C) measures 180 days from the UA date'
failures.explanation: Identified with the early-expiry consequence (C-034 passed) but rated Critical rather than High.

process.obs: The assignment refers to a 'negotiation playbook' and 'client instructions', but neither exists among the five documents. The agent had to infer the Agent's positions from the term sheet, the executed Credit Agreement and its Exhibit F.
Read the transmittal email, the markup and the Credit Agreement in full in 26KB chunks (steps 3-18), and handled the missing [TK] comments and the mixed tracked-change conventions explicitly.

When Exhibit F of the executed Credit Agreement ('guaranty of payment') conflicted with the term sheet §V(a) ('payment and performance'), it treated the executed agreement as controlling and conceded the borrower's point, without flagging the conflict as one for the client to decide.
Pursued a 'meet in the middle' posture: 11 counter-proposals, several of which gave ground the Agent's own documents did not require (Guarantor amendment consent, statute-of-limitations waiver).
43 steps, with several regenerate/validate cycles of the redline (steps 19-42) to get the tracked-change mechanics right.

failures.title: Redline restores guaranty scope to cover both 'payment and performance'
failures.source: facility-term-sheet.docx §V(a): 'shall provide an unconditional and irrevocable guaranty of payment and performance of all Obligations'; vs credit-agreement.docx Exhibit F §1: 'This is a guaranty of payment and not merely of collection'
failures.deliverable: WCS-5: 'Deletion of 'and performance' in Sections 2.1 and 2.2 accepted, consistent with Section 1 of Exhibit F to the Credit Agreement'
failures.explanation: The agent saw both sources and resolved the conflict for the executed Exhibit F (payment only) over the term sheet (payment and performance), accepting the guarantor's deletion. The expert treats the term sheet as the deal and expects 'performance' to be restored.

failures.title: Redline rejects the requirement that Guarantor consent is needed for amendments
failures.source: guaranty-agreement-initial-draft.docx §11.1: 'No consent of the Guarantor shall be required for any amendment...'; credit-agreement.docx §9.01: 'no consent of the Guarantor shall be required for amendments to this Agreement'
failures.deliverable: §11.1: 'No amendment ... that would increase, expand, or otherwise add to the obligations ... shall be effective without the written consent of the Guarantor' (WCS-24 counter-proposal)
failures.explanation: The agent read §9.01 but offered a limited Guarantor consent right as a compromise. The expert's lender-side position is outright rejection.

failures.title: Redline maintains that amendments require only the consent of the Administrative Agent at the direction of the Required Lenders
failures.source: initial draft §11.1; credit-agreement.docx §9.01
failures.deliverable: Same §11.1 counter-proposal adding Guarantor consent for obligation-increasing amendments
failures.explanation: This is the same concession as C018 viewed from the other side: the Agent-plus-Required-Lenders standard was not kept intact.

failures.title: Redline accepts or proposes a de minimis dollar-threshold carve-out for intercompany-debt subordination
failures.source: markup-transmittal-email.eml item 6: 'only Intercompany Indebtedness exceeding $5,000,000 in the aggregate is subject to subordination'
failures.deliverable: WCS-17: 'Not accepted; full subordination reinstated' (gave ground instead on the Section 8.2 payment block)
failures.explanation: Here the agent was firmer than the expert. It rejected any de minimis tranche because the $5M would be payable during default or insolvency, and conceded on payment-blockage timing instead. The rubric expects a reduced threshold as the counter. No document dictates either answer.

failures.title: Redline restores the waiver of statute-of-limitations defenses in Section 3
failures.source: facility-term-sheet.docx §V(f)(v): waiver of 'defenses arising under any applicable statute of limitations'; initial draft §3.4
failures.deliverable: WCS-11: 'We accept that the New York statute of limitations applies and have not reinstated the blanket waiver (recognizing the limits of N.Y. GOL 17-103 on pre-accrual waivers)'
failures.explanation: The agent knew the term sheet required the waiver but conceded on its own reading of GOL §17-103. The expert expects the waiver restored, as the term sheet requires (to the extent the law permits).

failures.title: Cover note explains the agent's position on guaranty scope (payment and performance)
failures.source: facility-term-sheet.docx §V(a) 'payment and performance'
failures.deliverable: Cover note items 5-7: 'Accepted ... Consistent with Section 1 of Exhibit F (guaranty of payment)'
failures.explanation: This follows from C001. The cover note explains why the agent accepted payment-only, the opposite of the position the rubric wants explained.

process.obs: Read the partner email and both credit-agreement excerpts in full (steps 4-9) before drafting, and caught real cross-document conflicts: the DIP cap, the 91-day maturity-floor date error, and the purchase price.

Took the partner's 'Draft it cleanly and don't hedge' (adequate protection) and 'Draft the automatic release broadly' literally. Its bracketed notes therefore stayed silent on enforceability and uptier risk, which the task's 'flag conflicts' mandate would have covered.

Drafted the agreement in six chunk files (steps 13-18) with one patch script and one validation (steps 19-20). No review pass for market and litigation risks absent from the documents (Serta, Ion Media).
Notes focus on conflicts between documents; issues the documents leave unaddressed (revolver vs term loan priority, the narrower Second Lien Obligations) got no note.

failures.title: ISSUE_002: Identifies revolver and term loan priority/pari passu question
failures.source: partner-drafting-instructions.eml §1: '$310 million first lien term loan + $55 million first lien revolving credit facility'; first-lien CA §2.18 'Third, ratably to pay ... Term Loans, Revolving Loans (other than Protective Advances)'
failures.deliverable: absent (waterfall defers to FL CA ordering; §2.5 only acknowledges revolving nature)
failures.explanation: The agent saw both facilities and the FL CA waterfall, and apparently treated the ratable ordering in FL CA §2.18 as settling the point. It never flagged that the instructions are silent on revolver super-priority. Arguably low value given §2.18, but the rubric requires the flag.

failures.title: ISSUE_004: Flags risk of automatic release enabling uptier/Serta-style transactions
failures.source: general legal knowledge (Serta Simmons/Boardriders liability-management transactions); partner email §8 'Draft the automatic release broadly'
failures.deliverable: absent; §5.1 note only says the payoff proviso stops Caldwell Reed arguing the clause could strip liens on a refinancing
failures.explanation: The agent followed the instruction to draft the release broadly and added only a payoff proviso. It never raised the risk of non-pro-rata uptier or lien stripping, which comes from market knowledge, not the documents.

failures.title: ISSUE_004: Considers anti-Serta protections for automatic release
failures.source: general legal knowledge (Serta/Boardriders; non-affiliate sale and ratable-benefit conditions)
failures.deliverable: absent; §5.1 has no non-affiliate or ratable-treatment condition
failures.explanation: Same gap as C-008: no anti-uptier conditions drafted or recommended.

failures.title: ISSUE_006: Flags enforceability risk of complete adequate protection cash payment waiver
failures.source: partner-drafting-instructions.eml §6(b): 'No cash adequate protection payments to the second lien. Period. ... Draft it cleanly and don't hedge.'; general law (11 U.S.C. §§361, 363(e), 364; Ion Media)
failures.deliverable: §6.3 note: 'Drafted without hedging, as instructed ... should be expected to draw Caldwell Reed's request for payment of their advisors' fees'
failures.explanation: The agent read 'don't hedge' as a ban on even an internal enforceability flag. The expert wants the draft kept clean but a note warning that a total adequate-protection waiver may not hold up in bankruptcy court.

failures.title: ISSUE_006: Recommends savings clause or limitation rather than complete waiver
failures.source: general legal knowledge (savings/enforceability carve-outs for adequate protection waivers)
failures.deliverable: absent; 6.3(c) is a complete waiver; the 6.5(d) backstop covers plan voting only
failures.explanation: No savings clause or softening was proposed for the cash adequate-protection waiver. This follows directly from the literal reading of the partner's instruction.

failures.title: ISSUE_010: Notes second lien does not include hedging/cash management
failures.source: second-lien-credit-agreement-excerpts.docx §1.01: '"Second Lien Obligations" means all Obligations ... under ... this Agreement and the Second Lien Loan Documents, including all principal, interest, fees, premiums...'; '"Second Lien Secured Parties" means the Administrative Agent, the Collateral Agent, and the Lenders'
failures.deliverable: absent; ICA defines Second Lien Obligations by cross-reference only; the related note (item 12) concerns the SL CA's narrow definition of First Lien Obligations
failures.explanation: The agent read the SL CA and spotted the asymmetry in how the SL CA defines First Lien Obligations. It never noted the mirror point that the second lien itself has no hedging or cash-management obligations or counterparties.

process.obs: Read all eight documents in full, in overlapping head/tail chunks (steps 3-15), including the xlsx through openpyxl.
Picked the filing date '[21] May 2025' without basis: the latest dated document is May 17, 2025 and no document gives a filing date.
Built the 12.5k-word application in six script parts with several sed cross-reference fixes (steps 17-33), validating once at the end.

failures.title: Correct filing date (May 20, 2025)
failures.source: No document states a filing date; latest dates are competitive-impact-memo.docx and zenith-financial-summary.xlsx 'Date: May 17, 2025'; demand chain: May 16, 2025 deadline
failures.deliverable: '[21] May 2025' (bracketed placeholder)
failures.explanation: May 20, 2025 does not appear in or follow from the documents; the rubric hard-codes a date the agent could not derive. The agent's bracketed date is a reasonable placeholder for a filing that has not yet happened.

failures.title: Notes simultaneous filing of Request for Arbitration
failures.source: general knowledge: ICC Rules Appendix V Art. 1(6) (Request for Arbitration within 10 days of the Secretariat's receipt of the Application); usual practice is to file both together
failures.deliverable: 'No Request for Arbitration ... has been filed ... Pinnacle undertakes to file its Request for Arbitration within ten days ... as required by Article 1(6) of Appendix V.'
failures.explanation: The agent's sequencing is legally permitted, but it chose filing the Request for Arbitration afterwards over the simultaneous filing the expert expects. This is a strategy difference, not an error of fact.

process.obs: Dumped the draft 10-Q in sed line ranges. Two reads spilled (steps 9-10); it re-flattened the table whitespace and re-read lines 791-1200 (steps 11-14), so the notes, including Note 13, were seen.
Wrote findings as structured data (findings.py) with a fixed severity field and generated the memo from it. It never cross-checked the severities against the materiality of each item.
Treated the dividend correctly as a recognized Q3 event (Finding 11) and Note 13 as a separate 'refresh' item (Finding 22), so the two were never linked.

failures.title: Classifies share count discrepancy as Minor
failures.source: draft-form-10q.docx cover: 'As of November 1, 2024, the registrant had 79,350,000 shares'; balance sheet / Note 11: 79,450,000; prior-quarter excerpts: 'Cover page shares outstanding (erroneous): 79,350,000; Correct: 79,450,000'
failures.deliverable: 'Finding 3. Shares outstanding on cover page are understated (79,350,000 vs. 79,450,000) [High]'
failures.explanation: Correctly identified but rated High, second of four tiers, against the expert's lowest tier. The FAIL clause names only Critical, so the rubric is slightly ambiguous, but High plainly does not meet the PASS condition.

failures.title: Notes the subsequent events note contradiction regarding dividend
failures.source: draft-form-10q.docx Note 13: 'determined that no events have occurred that require disclosure'; MD&A: 'The Company declared a quarterly dividend of $0.16 per share on September 28, 2024, payable on October 25, 2024'
failures.deliverable: Finding 22: 'The note concludes that there are no reportable subsequent events. Before filing, confirm ... payment of the October 25, 2024 dividend'
failures.explanation: Both facts were in the agent's output and both appear in the memo, but Finding 22 presents Note 13 as a routine refresh rather than calling out the contradiction with the undisclosed dividend.

process.obs: Read all five documents in full (steps 2-8) before drafting, then built the ACA and memo in four script parts (steps 10-16) and rendered both to PDF to check length.

Wrote the Permitted Servicer Instructions list (§3.4) from the Servicing Agreement's investment, transfer, fee and reserve mechanics, never re-checking it item by item against the five-item list in Indenture §3.01(b).
Cover-memo entries describe what changed and cite the source but often skip the rationale. The partner's own rationale was available to reuse.

failures.title: ISSUE_010: Cover memo explains reversal of successor approval right
failures.source: drafting-instructions-email.eml 'Successor Approval Right': 'This is backwards. The outgoing bank shouldn't get a veto over its replacement. The approval right runs to the Indenture Trustee, as the secured party representing the noteholders.'
failures.deliverable: Memo item 6: 'The form required any successor to be "reasonably acceptable to" Sovereign. That provision is deleted. Crestline selects and appoints the successor ... The outgoing bank has no consent or objection right.'
failures.explanation: The memo flags the departure and describes the new mechanics but never says why: that the secured party acting for the noteholders should control succession. That rationale was available verbatim in the instructions. The judge is somewhat strict, but the 'explains the rationale' element is missing.

failures.title: ACA provides Servicer pre-ECN authority to instruct deposits into Collection Account
failures.source: base-indenture-excerpts.docx §3.01(b): 'Prior to the delivery of an Exclusive Control Notice ... the Servicer shall have the right to instruct the Securities Intermediary ... to (i) deposit funds into the Trust Accounts, (ii) invest ...'
failures.deliverable: absent; §3.4(a) Permitted Servicer Instructions list only (i) investments, (ii) Collection-to-Distribution transfers, (iii) Servicer Fee, (iv) Reserve Release Certificates, (v) countersigned other
failures.explanation: The agent transposed Indenture §3.01(b) into ACA §3.4 but dropped the first item (deposits). It read the source in full at step 5.

process.obs: Converted all ~9,300 DMS files to text in a background job and searched them with rg for 'portfolio company', 'add-on', 'bolt-on' and 'tuck-in' (steps 4-27). Recall was complete: all 6 expected matters found.

Chose an inclusive scope: counted non-consummated deals (1006-00003, 1007-00002, 1011-00005) and a VC/growth-backed client with conflicting sponsor references (1008-00008) as qualifying, flagging them in the table instead of excluding them.
Wrote response.md with an unquoted-dollar heredoc (step 61), so the shell stripped most '$N' amounts (e.g., 'Headline value 0.0M (4.0M cash...)', 'Totals ~40M'). It never re-read the file to verify.
63 steps, a long per-matter verification phase (steps 37-60) reading engagement letters, closing certificates and funds flows.

failures.title: Qualifying set — precision
failures.source: DMS: 1006-00003 matter-dormancy-memorandum (SPA never signed); 1007-00002 auction postponed indefinitely (Dkt. 309); 1011-00005 dormant, LOI exclusivity lapsed; 1008-00008 sponsor not named, other Lumos files cite 'Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP'/growth-equity holders
failures.deliverable: 'The DMS holds 10 buy-side add-on acquisition matters' including 1006-00003, 1007-00002, 1011-00005 (marked 'Not consummated') and 1008-00008 ('Flag: confirm ... whether Lumos counts as PE-backed')
failures.explanation: The agent saw the dormancy and non-closing facts and the sponsor ambiguity, and labelled them, but still counted these four matters in the qualifying set. The expert's set excludes deals that never happened and non-PE-backed clients, so this is a scope and threshold call, not a retrieval miss.

process.obs: Read the ICF, IRB letter, protocol (two halves) and the checklist workbook in full (steps 4-9), and also unzipped the docx headers and footers (steps 10-11).

Took the checklist's 'N/A — Not a federal regulatory requirement' / CIRB determination as the frame and rated the COI item 'Low (advisory)'. It gave only a risk rationale and dropped the checklist's own 'Institutional Policy / AAHRPP' label.

failures.title: Issue 4: References best-practice standards for COI disclosure
failures.source: fda-inspection-checklist.xlsx row 17: 'Institutional Policy / AAHRPP — Disclosure of investigator financial conflicts of interest to participants'
failures.deliverable: D-22: 'The CIRB does not require disclosure, so this is not a regulatory deficiency, but it is a likely inspection and litigation vulnerability.'
failures.explanation: The checklist the agent read labels this row 'Institutional Policy / AAHRPP', but the report justifies the COI disclosure only as an inspection or litigation risk. It cites no AAHRPP, institutional-policy or research-ethics standard.
